programme.title: Disco: Soundtrack of a Revolution
programme.desc: At the end of the 1970s, the founding principles of disco – queerness, diversity and feminism – were coming under increasing attack from a predominantly white, straight, rock-loving audience. By the summer of 1978, disco appeared untouchable, but mass marketing and rampant commercialism were beginning to turn the tide. A glut of bad disco singles and the perceived elitism of clubs like Studio 54 fuelled a surge in anti-disco feeling. This is the story of how disco died - and where it went.

programme.title: Sounds of the Seventies
programme.desc: Disco was all pervasive in the mid and early 70s. And while towards the end of the decade punk stole the headlines, disco still had the high street. Everyone was into it and getting down on it at the local discotheque. Join us in a celebration of all things disco including performances by The Jacksons, Thelma Houston, Sylvester, Carl Douglas, George McCrae, Sister Sledge, McFadden and Whitehead, Eruption and Gloria Gaynor.

programme.title: Top of the Pops

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: David Hamilton presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 29 July 1979 and featuring Thin Lizzy, Chanter Sisters, Liverpool Express, Jimmy James and the Vagabonds and dance sequences from Ruby Flipper.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: Jamie Theakston presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 7 July 2000 and featuring Kylie Minogue, Lonyo, Samantha Mumba, Coldplay, Vengaboys, Sid Owen, Robbie Williams, Five & Queen and Eminem.

programme.title: Fungi: The Web of Life
programme.desc: Much of life on earth is connected by a vast, hidden network that we are only just beginning to understand. Out of sight, between the world of plants and animals, another realm exists - the kingdom of fungi. Passionate biologist and writer Merlin Sheldrake travels the globe, exploring the secret world of fungi. Through dazzling images of fungi under the microscope and all around us in the forest, Merlin unravels the many secrets of these essential organisms. So much more than mushrooms, not only do fungi shape the weather and support life on land, they are also at the cutting edge of medical research and even have the power to break down plastic waste. This film takes us from the ancient Tasmanian Tarkine rainforest to the mystical wilds of China’s Yunnan Province, in search of solutions to some of our planet’s biggest challenges. Can the answers be found in the wonderful world of fungi?

programme.title: Full Circle with Michael Palin
programme.desc: Michael Palin undertakes a journey around the Pacific Rim through 18 countries. Arriving in Qingdao, Michael checks into his hotel - which is curiously like a Bavarian castle - and finds himself in a room that was once Chairman Mao's. Having climbed China's holiest mountain, he travels to Shanghai to see the new face of the nation, then takes a steamboat trip on the Yangtze River

programme.title: Miss Marple

programme.title: Fanny and Alexander
programme.desc: Ingmar Bergman’s dreamlike chronicle of an extended family in early 20th-century Sweden. One tumultuous year in the life of the Ekdahl family is viewed through the eyes of ten-year-old Alexander, whose imagination fuels the magical goings-on leading up to and following the death of his father. When his mother marries a stern bishop, Alexander and his sister Fanny are banished to a gothic world.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Film-maker Ingmar Bergman shows us his world on the desolate and mysterious Baltic island of Faro. In his home at the seashore, he talks about the childhood that shaped him and speaks of how the art of film was often a comfort to him. He tells, too, of love and death, and lists his worst demons.

programme.desc: On one of the wettest days in Roadshow history, over 2,000 visitors queue to see Fiona Bruce and the experts sheltering under the canopy at Minehead station, which is run by West Somerset Railway. Objects brought to camera include a bracelet made from jewels once owned by the last of the Romanovs, the Russian royal family, photographs from the day The Beatles came to film A Hard Day's Night and a bronze by sculptor Rodin.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds and Power: The Story of the Village
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson unlocks the ancient roots of the Northumberland village of Warkworth. With the help of locals, he discovers clues that point back almost 1,000 years to the Norman conquest when the invaders laid the foundations of a planned community, still visible to this day.

programme.title: Shakespeare: Rise of a Genius
programme.desc: Shakespeare’s life and legacy is threatened when the Gunpowder Plot unearths a secret he has worked all his life to bury: his family are Catholics, traitors to the crown. When his daughter is implicated in the fallout, Shakespeare unleashes his most epic work to date: Macbeth, which appeals to the new monarch, King James I. As Shakespeare teeters towards death, he reflects on his successes and failures, questioning family, forgiveness and mortality as his work is at risk of being lost forever.

programme.title: The BBC Television Shakespeare
programme.desc: A set of television adaptations of all 37 plays by William Shakespeare.

programme.title: Peace in No Man's Land
programme.desc: The story of the Christmas truce On Christmas Eve 1914 on the Western Front, British and German soldiers sang carols to each other across a frosty, moonlit No Man's Land. The next morning, on Christmas Day, hundreds of men of both nations emerged from the trenches to talk, joke, take photographs and exchange souvenirs, in the most famous fraternisation of the First World War. This remarkable event is remembered by three soldiers who took part: Graham Williams of the London Rifle Brigade, Leslie Walkinton of the Queen's Westminster Rifles and Albert Moren of The Queen's Regiment.

programme.title: Alaska: Earth's Frozen Kingdom
programme.desc: Three-part series that looks at a year in Alaska, revealing the stories of pioneering Alaskans, both animal and human, as they battle the elements and reap the benefits of nature's seasonal gold rush.

programme.title: The Story of Scottish Art
programme.desc: The story of Scottish art and its impact on the international art world is celebrated in this four-part series presented by acclaimed artist Lachlan Goudie. The series spans 5,000 years of Scotland's history, from the earliest Neolithic art to the present day. In the first programme, Lachlan explores Scotland's earliest art. He visits the Ring of Brodgar in Orkney, where standing stones have watched the seasons pass for thousands of years. On the island of Westray he encounters an ancient figurine - the Westray Wife - the oldest sculpted human figure in the British Isles. He explores the sophisticated art of the Picts and the Gaels, the exuberant Renaissance period of the early Stewart kings, and the destructive heights of the Reformation, when religious artworks were all but wiped out in Scotland.

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the quiz programme from Surrey University. The specialist subjects are the novels of Anthony Powell, the Byzantine Empire in the age of Justinian, the life and works of Giuseppe Verdi and WE Gladstone.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Panel game of word definitions and deceptions hosted by Robert Robinson. Team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by Arthur Marshall, David Hunt, Pauline Collins and Gabrielle Drake.

programme.title: John Berger: The Art of Looking
programme.desc: Film exploring the life and work of the late writer and art critic John Berger. The film is an intimate portrait of a man who has shaped our understanding of the concept of seeing.

programme.title: Metalworks!
programme.desc: Dan Cruickshank visits Britain's finest country houses, museums and factories as he uncovers the 18th- and 19th-century fascination with silver. Delving into an unsurpassed era of shimmering opulence, heady indulgence and conspicuous consumption, Dan discovers the Georgian and Victorian obsession with this tantalising precious metal which represented status, wealth and excellent taste. He gives us a glimpse of some of the most extensive collections and exquisite pieces of silverware to have ever been made on British shores.

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: Janina Ramirez and Alastair Sooke discover the art and design of Amsterdam - a city that pioneered much of modern life, from multinational trade to how we design our homes.

programme.title: Clive Myrie's African Adventure
programme.desc: In the second leg of his Ghanaian adventure, Clive heads 80 miles from the capital city of Accra to the picturesque fishing ports of Cape Coast and Elmina, where he digs deep into his ancestral roots. He takes part in one of Ghana's most exciting tribal celebrations as he’s welcomed by the Fante people. He's given a new name by elders from the group, as well as a personalised Fante flag that celebrates both his West African and Jamaican roots. As part of this journey, Clive makes a difficult but moving visit to a former slave fort to discover some of what his ancestors went through. And, in a personal first, Clive gets to dance in a hip-hop video with rising star Kojo Vypa.

programme.title: Newsday

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Nawal Al-Maghafi reports from Yemen's front lines, where Houthi forces are posing the most serious threat in years to the city of Taiz, raising fears of a major escalation in a conflict that has endured for more than a decade. We also trace the roots of Yemen's war, exploring how the country's strategic location has drawn it into a struggle involving Saudi Arabia, Iran and the United States. Plus: BBC Mundo travels to Panama's Coiba Island, a biodiversity hotspot, to explore how a former prison colony helped preserve a rare and fragile natural world.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: Can the great outdoors still inspire a generation raised on screens? 2026 sees the Duke of Edinburgh Awards marking 70 years of taking young people on adventures in the British countryside. To celebrate, explorer Dwayne Fields travels from expeditions in the Yorkshire Dales to adrenaline-fuelled outings in the Scottish Highlands, meeting the people proving that real-life adventures are more fulfilling than their digital equivalents.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded examines the growing role of artificial intelligence in the US midterm elections. From AI-generated political adverts and deepfake videos to chatbot election advice and algorithm-driven feeds, AI is now embedded in every stage of the information ecosystem. Political campaigns are using AI to create content faster and cheaper than ever before. At the same time, convincing fake videos, synthetic ads and coordinated bot networks are making it harder for voters to separate fact from fiction. With millions of people now turning to chatbots for political information, are we entering an era where AI doesn't just influence elections, but shapes how voters understand them?

programme.desc: Shiona McCallum meets the mums and hospital staff trialling the first new assisted birth innovation in decades. Paul Carter finds out how technology powering advanced prosthetics is also helping train humanoid robots. Ammie Sekhon finds out why medical students are practicing with AI-powered virtual patients. And Adrienne Murray explores how new 3D imaging is being used to support heart procedures.

programme.title: Talking Movies
programme.desc: Talking Movies looks at the films that made waves at the BFI London Film Festival and the New York Film Festival in October. Tom Brook explores the film Elsinore, which contains a magnetic performance from Andrew Scott portraying the actor Ian Charleson, and is already being tipped for Oscar glory. Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine also made a big impression and we talk to the director as well as the cast from the festival red carpet. Wedaeli Chibelushi offers her thoughts on the new African drama Congo Boy and Emma Jones looks at Spanish film La Bola Negra, which has been earning rave reviews and is being talked about as a serious contender for the Best Film category at Academy Awards in 2027. Plus, we head to the USA for a look at the New York Film Festival which opened with the crime drama Paper Tiger. Other standout films there included the documentary Once Upon A Time in Harlem and Mike Leigh's Tender Loving Care.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: This week the BBC announced more cuts as part of its drive to save £500 million, following on from a series of other budget saving measures over the last few months. Katie and Ros take stock of everything announced so far along with a panel of experts: ex-BBC executive Roger Mosey, MP for Southport Patrick Hurley, Baroness Morgan, former Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport and the BBC Deputy Director General Rhodri Talfan-Davies. And a new Channel 4 programme investigates public attitudes toward disability. The creators of The Experiment have built a fictional care home for disabled people and invite members of the public into the facility to see if they can recognise Nazi-era concepts disguised as modern social care. Producer Nick Parnes and presenter Sophie Morgan join the show.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Why are record amounts of money pouring into sport? The LA Lakers are starting the new NBA as the most expensive sports team in history after being bought for $12.5bn. Record sums have also been spent on the NFL's Seattle Seahawks and English Premier League teams Liverpool and Chelsea in recent weeks. Is it really being driven by the search for an AI proof investment? Sal Galatioto is the man billionaires call when they want to buy or sell a sports team and he explains why the prices keep on climbing. Leading TV sports rights executive Daniel Cohen, of Octagon Global Media Consulting, explains the impact this is all having on how we watch and how much we pay. Ben Thompson also hears from the billionaire founder and CEO of Fanatics, Michael Rubin, and how fans are continuing to splash out on replica shirts, trading cards and other merchandise.

programme.title: Talking Movies

Tom Brook explores the film Elsinore, which contains a magnetic performance from Andrew Scott portraying the actor Ian Charleson, and is already being tipped for Oscar glory. Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine also made a big impression and we talk to the director as well as the cast from the festival red carpet. Wedaeli Chibelushi offers her thoughts on the new African drama Congo Boy and Emma Jones looks at Spanish film La Bola Negra, which has been earning rave reviews and is being talked about as a serious contender for the Best Film category at Academy Awards in 2027. Plus, we head to the USA for a look at the New York Film Festival which opened with the crime drama Paper Tiger. Other standout films there included the documentary Once Upon A Time in Harlem and Mike Leigh's Tender Loving Care.

programme.desc: In the second leg of his Ghanaian adventure, Clive heads 80 miles from the capital city of Accra to the picturesque fishing ports of Cape Coast and Elmina, where he digs deep into his ancestral roots. He takes part in one of Ghana's most exciting tribal celebrations as he’s welcomed by the Fante people. He's given a new name by elders from the group, as well as a personalised Fante flag that celebrates both his West African and Jamaican roots. As part of this journey, Clive makes a difficult but moving visit to a former slave fort to discover some of what his ancestors went through. And, in a personal first, Clive gets to dance in a hip-hop video with rising star Kojo Vypa.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: Nigella continues to show us that what and how we cook really can make us feel better and more alive. She introduces us to her favourite recipes for sharing with family and friends. Whether it's a tray of nourishing breakfast bars for those mornings you all need to grab and go; a supper of crunchy chicken cutlets that are just as much fun in the making as in the eating; or Nigella's latest addition to her 'Chocolate Cake Hall of Fame' - her stunning dark and sumptuous chocolate cake, every recipe is a guaranteed crowd pleaser. There's a pork bun feast, too. First inspired by a visit to a New York eatery, Nigella's succulent belly pork burgers - with their array of condiments and picky bits - are now a favourite DIY lunch when the hoards descend.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: A stone’s throw from today’s antiques fair in West Sussex is a 500-acre wild botanic garden with an exquisite Elizabethan mansion at its centre. Natasha Raskin Sharp takes a break from the hustle and bustle of the fair to visit Kew Wakehurst and learn of its long history. The mansion’s roof has just been restored, and inside Natasha meets one of the curators to find out about several objects recently uncovered that tell of this grand house’s story. Over the fence, niece and aunt Abby and Della take on dad and daughter Sonal and Ruhi on a sweep of the antiques stalls, with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester in tow. With a few buys under their belts, the reds recline on a pair of furry blue armchairs, but the punchy price tag means they don’t stop for long. The blues also have furniture on their minds when Ruhi spots an occasional table – made from a tree trunk. In Chichester, the teams plan to grow a profit when Nick Hall takes to the rostrum. Caroline hopes her bonus buy will bring Abby and Della good luck, while Thomas aims to spread the love with his.

Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Ian, Kate, Paul and Suzy – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel. The film follows one mother who begins the year planning a future with her daughter, only to see it end with a promise to avenge her daughter’s death. After she publicly blamed the Iranian authorities, she was forced to flee the country and live in exile. A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death. Filmed both inside and outside the country, this is the raw and uncompromising story of a year in Iran, told by some of the people who were there.

programme.desc: Behind the billion-pound success of OnlyFans lies a hidden ecosystem of exploitation. A BBC Current Affairs investigation uncovers allegations of exploitation, coercion and violence committed by some of the hundreds of agents who manage many of the platform’s creators as well as the potential for modern slavery. Through survivor testimony, undercover access to a managers’ chat forum and expert legal analysis, the film exposes an industry where young women are trapped, threatened and profited from - raising urgent questions about accountability at the heart of one of Britain's most lucrative tech companies.

She is therefore overjoyed when he asks her to help him store some wares in a lock-up garage. A job at the local bowls club gives Kurtan a new sense of purpose, but when Kerry entangles Kurtan in her new venture, things start to unravel, and the Mucklowe family loyalties are put to the test.

programme.desc: Georgie’s best mate Vicky is the ultimate dating ice queen. Vicky is super-picky, has a long list of unrealistic criteria for her perfect match, dumps guys for using the wrong emojis, analyses everything they do and walks out of 60 per cent of her dates. Tired of hearing about Vicky’s first date failures and delivering advice that gets ignored, Georgie calls on sex and relationships expert Oloni for an urgent intervention. Oloni wants Vicky to see where it's all going wrong, so she dishes out some cold, hard truths as she unpacks Vicky’s dating history and shows her some frank and honest video feedback from friends, family and even exes, to prove to Vicky that her bad dating behaviour needs a serious reboot. Oloni has to pull out all the stops to melt this ice queen as she sets Vicky up on a series of first dates that will challenge her behaviour and make her a better dater. Under the watchful eye of Oloni and Georgie, is Vicky ready for a change, will she give the guys a chance, be nice and let her guard down, or will she retain her ice queen crown?

Britpop was still booming, with Oasis continuing to dominate singles sales with Sleeper hot on their heels. The ramble is returning for its 12th year, set against the stunning backdrop of the Peak District. The presenters walk alongside five remarkable young people who have faced significant challenges, hearing first-hand how BBC Children in Need-funded projects have helped them build confidence, resilience and hope for the future.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Aberdeenshire, visiting Scotland’s first inclusive farm, built by a blind farmer who is determined to make agriculture accessible for all. Arlene sails to Jura to see how the locals cope with the huge deer population and find new outlets for venison. Anne discovers how the shortage of affordable rural housing is being tackled in the Highlands. And Shahbaz is on the shores of Loch Linnhe near Fort William to see the stranded fishing boat that has become a local landmark.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek is island-hopping in this round-up of his favourite Welsh island walks. He goes wild in west Wales as he sails to Skomer Island – a national nature reserve of international importance due to its seabirds - where he gets a close-up view of the puffins, razorbills and guillemots before staying up late to see the Manx shearwater. Next, Derek goes to Flat Holm Island, where he braves a huge colony of seagulls and discovers more about the island's past, including some Victorian gun placements. Lastly, Derek heads up north to Wales's largest island, Anglesey, where he visits another tiny island with a secluded chapel, an unexpected motor racing track, a neolithic burial chamber and a sauna on a beach.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt dishes up a feast of food from the Saturday Kitchen archives to whet the appetite for the week ahead. The Hairy Bikers bring comfort food bang up to date with sticky Szechuan lamb, stuffed into pillowy soft bao buns, with a fresh hit of pickled carrots, spring onion and herbs – cosy comfort with a fragrant Asian twist! Meera Sodha introduces a taste of Sri Lanka to the studio as she continues the comfort theme with her warming lentil and coconut dal with crispy mustard kale. Jeremy Lee brings his effervescent charm and wit to the kitchen whilst giving an underused cut of meat its chance in the spotlight. He makes a rich steamed kid pudding that melts in the mouth. Mary McCartney celebrates Bonfire Night with her flavour-packed smoky dogs, while Carmen O’Neal and Idris Elba team up to serve a masterclass in brandy. And queen of puddings Nigella Lawson tucks into either her food heaven, scallops, or her food hell, candied fruit. Meanwhile, Rick Stein explores the New Forest's bounty of produce, and the Hairy Bikers make a Menorcan dish in the Mediterranean Sea.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means ‘to brew’) and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt’s restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine. With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences.

programme.title: Best Bakes Ever
programme.desc: With Britain more obsessed with baking than ever, actress and cake expert Jane Asher brings together a selection of recipes from the nation's favourite television chefs, for Best Bakes Ever. Each episode gives baking fans another chance to experience classic dishes from the likes of the James Martin, Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, the Hairy Bikers, Raymond Blanc, Nigella Lawson, Tom Kerridge, Lorraine Pascale and Rachel Khoo. There's added insight and appreciation from Jane herself too. Whether its cakes, pies, puddings or main courses - this greatest hits of baking is a must for anyone with a need to knead, and should help inspire even more of us to start getting creative in the kitchen.

programme.title: I Was Monty's Double
programme.desc: World War II drama. A low-ranking officer who resembles General Montgomery is recruited to play his double in an elaborate plan to trick the Nazis.

programme.title: Women's Super League
programme.desc: Women's Super League action as Charlton Athletic face Chelsea.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin introduces a collection of the best finds from the show's travels to Lulworth Castle in Dorset, Chiddingstone Castle in Kent, and Wrest Park in Bedfordshire. The antiques experts include Catherine Southon, Christina Trevanion, Adam Partridge, Mark Stacey and Thomas Plant, with items ranging from a cloisonne vase to an astonishing collection of First World War slides. Paul also finds out more about the ancient art of shipbuilding at Buckler's Hard in Hampshire.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: For a live demonstration of terroir, Eva heads to Domaine Dujac, home of the current most-wanted Burgundy wine. Standing on one side of a road, owner Jeremy Seysses points to a parcel of grand cru (the very best) of Clos de la Roche. On the other side is a premier cru (the next best) - a Gevrey-Chambertin Combottes. Back at the winery, Eva tucks into beef cheeks bathed in Domaine Dujac for a classic boeuf bourguignon lunch. Despite the grapes being grown just a few metres away, these reds are a class apart.

programme.title: Wild Horses, the Rockies and Me
programme.desc: Gordon Buchanan heads to the Rocky Mountains in search of wild horses. Finding two stallions battling over a herd, Gordon immerses himself in their world, hoping to win their trust.

programme.title: BBC Young Musician
programme.desc: Who will be crowned the winner? Three virtuosic performers vie for the coveted title in a thrilling concert at Bristol Beacon. Presented by Petroc Trelawny.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob are back in Norfolk - a bittersweet return, as this was the very first location where Ted joined them. They both reminisce about Ted and raise a cup in his memory - although Ted would have preferred a biscuit. They head to some prime Norfolk lakes, hoping to catch a bream. It’s been well documented that Bob is not a fan of the bream, but will a big catch make him change his tune? It's Paul and Bob's birthday week, and they consider whether they may celebrate any further milestones or simply let them pass. Bob ends up throwing a surprise 70s-themed birthday party for Paul on the roof of the Blickling Estate, once owned by the Boleyn family.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Irish film star Chris O'Dowd joins Bill Murray and his friend Tom Coyne for a lively round of golf, with enthusiasm occasionally outstripping ability. Away from the fairways, a traditional rambling house takes Bill outside his comfort zone as he explores Ireland's rich storytelling traditions. Later, in a packed Irish pub, the music starts – and staying on the sidelines proves impossible.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland

programme.title: Walk the Line

Featuring an appearance from Asim Chaudry.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Following this week’s Labour Budget, Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Warwick. On the panel are chief secretary to the treasury, Labour’s Emma Reynolds MP; Conservative James Cartlidge MP; Liberal Democrat Daisy Cooper MP; Reform UK’s Zia Yusuf; and podcaster and author Alastair Campbell. They debate the Budget, Brexit and debt from student loans.

A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

Chef Suzie Lee reveals how top chefs are getting creative as they reduce food waste.

programme.desc: Marcus and Emma head to the Maldives on a rescue mission for an injured turtle. Back in Plymouth, Ian trains Zeus the zebra shark using a toy boat, and Andrew collects fresh seaweed for Larry the lobster.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head to Ipswich, where among the treasures they find are a duke's chamber pot now used to drink champagne from, one of the earliest record players, and a 50p find on a white elephant stall which turns out to be worth much more.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today Flog It! comes from Glemham Hall in the Suffolk countryside. Antiques experts James Lewis and David Fletcher find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. There’s a Flog It first when James uncovers a copy of a Raphael painting saved by a Jewish professor who fled Hitler’s regime, and David Fletcher spots a rare flintlock pistol. Paul Martin visits a Cold War airbase to find out what life was like for American airmen based in the UK.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Maisie Adam, Ade Edmondson, Rickie Haywood-Williams and Sammi Kinghorn take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Jonathan Head reports from Thailand, where recent flooding has highlighted the growing challenges facing Bangkok. As climate change brings rising seas and more extreme weather across South East Asia, we examine why the Thai capital is among the region's most vulnerable cities. Plus: BBC Eye investigates the shadow war being fought inside Russia, speaking to two Russian men who claim to have secretly worked for Ukraine's intelligence services. Through rare first-hand accounts, we explore a clandestine world of covert operations, sabotage and espionage targeting military personnel and infrastructure far from the battlefield.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc: In September 1972, one month after dictator Idi Amin announces his plan to expel all Ugandan Asians from the country, 80,000 people are making plans to flee, in fear for their lives. Maz and Bharti head for the capital Kampala, where hundreds gather, desperate to find out whether their British passports will be enough to escape to Britain. As the deadline approaches, Harminder’s father escapes arrest and schoolboy Paresh hides during overnight curfews while gunfire echoes across the city. Britain is divided. Controversial politician Enoch Powell rallies those who say the Ugandan Asians have no right to come, a newspaper poll finds just six per cent of the public want them here, and some councils try to steer new arrivals away from their cities. In Uganda, Amin refuses to negotiate – stepping up the pressure on those stuck in the country.

programme.title: Operation Ouch!
programme.desc: Dr Xand’s favourite cold virus is the rhinovirus: that’s one that gets right up your nose and gives you the sniffles. So when the doctors get a question in the lab asking why your nose runs when you have a cold, they decide to become rhinoviruses and attack the body’s defences through a giant nose. We also get a chance to see right inside Dr Xand’s nostrils when he sticks a camera up his nose to show Dr Chris a real-life, flapping bogey specimen - gross alert! Dr Ronx makes a whole class of schoolchildren forget where their elbows are with a mind-blowing body trick you can try on your friends, and in Ouch and About, Ethan wants to know which is the strongest bone in his body. Over in Australia, six-year-old Jakobi is flown by helicopter to Sydney by the Flying Doctors because his local hospital thinks he needs specialist care. Lucy goes to the hospital in Edinburgh to find out why she’s woken up with a swollen face. And in Liverpool, Michael’s foot has been run over by a car, so no surprise that he’s ended up in the emergency department. Ouch!

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: Did you know that the Victorians invented films? Not only that, but one of the first stars of the moving image was Queen Victoria! Using real footage recently restored by the BFI, this special show takes a Horribly Historical look at the Victorians’ obsession with film. We see some of Queen Vicky’s very first filmic appearances (also featuring an initially reluctant Tsar Nicholas I), and also how the Victorians became obsessed with filming everything, from their holidays abroad to strapping cameramen to the front of a moving train (using only ropes) to make ‘Phantom Ride’ films. Along the way we also meet the Lumiere brothers (one of whom looks a lot like First Dates' Fred Sirieix), Kaiser Wilhelm II, notable Victorian actor Herbert Beerbohm Tree, and we see that the Victorians were also early adopters of Fake News. The episode ends with a show-stopping song that traces the evolution of film from the Victorians’ first forays through to the blockbusters we see in the multiplexes today.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Plastic is one of the greatest inventions in human history. It makes so much of our lives possible, but how we dispose of it is now a massive problem. By the year 2050 it’s thought that there will be more plastic than fish in our seas. So what can we do about it? First, ditch the disposable plastic water bottle and go for tap water in a reusable bottle. Better for the environment and cheaper too! Next, join a beach clean. It may seem like this problem is too big for us to handle but many hands make light work. Reduce, reuse and, importantly, recycle. And even more importantly than that, don’t drop litter. A bag that is thrown on the streets of London could end up on the coast of Africa or in the belly of a whale or a turtle. Lastly and most importantly, know that every single person can make a difference. One single plastic bag could choke a turtle or sunfish. One plastic straw could be the end of a gorgeous, iconic animal, so know you have power and use it.

programme.desc: Tom Selznick (Elijah Wood) is the most talented pianist of his generation, but has stopped performing in public because of his stage fright.

programme.title: All Good Things
programme.desc: A love story and murder mystery inspired by the true story of the infamous missing persons case in New York.

programme.title: The Fiance
programme.desc: A couple’s hunting trip turns sinister as a strange transformation begins under a rising moon.

programme.title: Black Death
programme.desc: The year is 1348. Europe has fallen under the shadow of the Black Death. As the plague decimates all in its path, fear and superstition are rife.

programme.title: Bonnie & Clyde vs Dracula
programme.desc: Bonnie & Clyde meet the epic Vampire in this duel to the death.

programme.title: Man Finds Tape
programme.desc: After finding mysterious video clips, Lynn returns home to investigate a homicide and uncovers a disturbing secret in her Texas town.

programme.title: V/H/S
programme.desc: A group of misfits acquire a rare tape with terrifying footage and are confronted with a dead body.

programme.title: V/H/S 2
programme.desc: Mysterious VHS tapes with horrific contents are found in a missing student's abandoned house.

programme.title: V/H/S: Viral
programme.desc: A stream of police cars chasing after a deranged ice cream truck driver has captivated the attention of the greater Los Angeles area.

programme.title: Censor
programme.desc: Film censor Enid (Niamh Algar, Wrath of Man) is assigned to review a disturbing film that recalls her childhood memories. She begins to unravel how this eerie work might be tied to the long-ago disappearance of her sister.

programme.title: Heretic
programme.desc: Hannah, who speaks to spirits, meets a lost soul and uncovers a terrifying entity tied to her past.

programme.title: Amulet
programme.desc: Tomaz, an ex-soldier is living in a decaying house, inhabited by a young woman and her dying mother. He starts to fall for his new companion but cannot ignore his suspicion that something insidious might also be living alongside them.

programme.title: The Carpenter's Son
programme.desc: In this genre-bending thriller of spiritual warfare, a young Jesus is thrust into his first confrontation with demonic forces.

programme.title: You're All Gonna Die
programme.desc: A team investigates a case at an abandoned site, unaware they are being hunted by a killer.

programme.title: The ABCs of Death
programme.desc: A 26-chapter anthology that showcases death in all its vicious wonder and brutal beauty.

programme.title: The Abcs Of Death 2
programme.desc: 26 new stories about death from the next generation of genre filmmakers.

programme.title: Kiss of the Damned
programme.desc: Beautiful vampire Djuna tries to resist the advances of the handsome, human screenwriter Paolo, but eventually gives in to their passion.

programme.title: To the Wonder
programme.desc: A romantic drama about men and women grappling with love and its many phases and seasons.

programme.title: Little Men
programme.desc: When 13-year-old Jake's grandfather dies, his family moves from Manhattan back into his father's Brooklyn home.

programme.title: Ira & Abby
programme.desc: A hastily married couple quickly devolve into a life of affairs, meddling parents, and therapy.

programme.title: Humpday
programme.desc: It's been a decade since Ben (Duplass) and Andrew (Leonard) were the bad boys of their college campus. Ben has settled down and found a job, wife, and home.

programme.title: God Bless America
programme.desc: Frank (Joel Murray) has had enough of the downward spiral of American culture. Divorced, recently fired, and possibly terminally ill, Frank feels he has nothing left to live for.

programme.title: The Lost City
programme.desc: Veteran actor Andy Garcia steps into the director's chair for his first voyage into feature filmmaking with this heartfelt tribute to revolutionary, late-'50s-era Cuba featuring Dustin Hoffman.

programme.title: Rabbit Trap
programme.desc: A musician couple captures a sound not meant for human ears. Soon, a stranger knocks on their door and their reality begins to blur.

programme.title: The Wave (English dub)
programme.desc: The very day he’s about to drive his family to a new life in the city, geologist Kristian Elkjord senses something wrong with the mountain that overlooks his scenic town.

programme.title: Mayday
programme.desc: Ana joins an army of girls engaged in a never-ending war. Ana trains as a sharpshooter and discovers newfound freedom and courage. Though she finds strength, she comes to realize that she’s not the killer they want her to be.

programme.title: Marrowbone
programme.desc: Four young siblings vow to stay together when their mother dies. But when a ghostly presence torments them and a lawyer threatens their pact, the four must stand together or be torn apart forever.

programme.title: Nature Calls
programme.desc: Determined to honor his father's scouting legacy an Assistant Scoutmaster convinces a group of kids to secretly ditch a slumber party in favor of a weekend scout trip.

programme.title: Results
programme.desc: Recently divorced, newly rich, and utterly miserable, Danny [Kevin Corrigan] would seem to be the perfect test subject for a definitive look at the relationship between money and happiness.

programme.title: Honeymoon
programme.desc: A newlywed couple's idyllic country-lake honeymoon descends into chaos.

programme.title: Little Joe
programme.desc: Alice (Emily Beecham) has engineered a special flower that makes its owner happy. Against company policy, Alice takes one home to her son. As their plant grows, so does Alice's suspicion that her new creation may not be as harmless as they thought.

programme.title: The Assessment
programme.desc: In the near future, a couple's seven-day test to have a child becomes a psychological nightmare.

programme.title: White Bird In A Blizzard
programme.desc: Kat Connors' (Shailene Woodley) glamorous but strange mother Eve vanishes. Kat is excited by her new freedom but disturbing facts surface and the mystery begins to haunt her.

programme.title: In the Fade (English dub)
programme.desc: Golden Globe® Winner for best foreign language film. Katja’s family is killed in a terrorist attack and her life falls apart. The killers are set free and Katja can do nothing else but seek justice.

programme.title: Trap
programme.desc: A man and his teenage daughter realize they're at the center of a dark and sinister event while watching a concert.

programme.title: Papillon
programme.desc: The epic story of Henri Papillon Charrière, a safecracker from the Parisian underworld who is framed for murder and condemned to life in the notorious penal colony on Devil's Island. Determined to regain his freedom, Papillon forms an unlikely alliance with convicted counterfeiter Louis Dega, who in exchange for protection, agrees to finance Papillon's escape.

programme.title: A History of Violence
programme.desc: When a pair of petty criminals attempt to rob his small-town diner, Tom Stall (Viggo Mortensen) quickly and easily kills them both. In the flush of news coverage of Tom's seemingly heroic actions, a threatening stranger named Carl Fogarty (Ed Harris) comes to town, fingering the unassuming family man as long-missing Philadelphia mobster Joey Cusack. To the horror of his wife, Edie (Maria Bello), and teenage son, Jack (Ashton Holmes), Tom finds he must confront his violent past.

programme.title: Hitchcock
programme.desc: Following his great success with "North by Northwest," director Alfred Hitchcock makes a daring choice for his next project: an adaptation of Robert Bloch's novel "Psycho." When the studio refuses to back the picture, Hitchcock decides to pay for it himself in exchange for a percentage of the profits. His wife, Alma Reville, has serious reservations about the film but supports him nonetheless. Still, the production strains the couple's marriage.

programme.title: Enter Nowhere
programme.desc: Three strangers arrive one at a time in a remote cabin, and learn they have been brought together for a reason.

programme.title: Nerve
programme.desc: Industrious high school senior Vee Delmonico (Emma Roberts) is tired of living life on the sidelines. Pressured by her friends, Vee decides to join Nerve, a popular online game that challenges players to accept a series of dares. It's not long before the adrenaline-fueled competition requires her to perform increasingly dangerous stunts. When Nerve begins to take a sinister turn, Vee finds herself in a high-stakes finale that will ultimately determine her entire future.

programme.title: Beasts of the Southern Wild
programme.desc: Six-year-old Hushpuppy lives with her father, Wink, in a remote Delta community. Wink is a stern taskmaster, but he is preparing his young daughter for the end of the world. When Wink falls mysteriously ill, nature seems to fall ill with him. Temperatures rise, the ice caps melt, and fearsome prehistoric beasts called aurochs run loose. Rising waters threaten to engulf their community, sending Hushpuppy in search of her long-lost mother.

programme.title: The Hobbit
programme.desc: An animated adaptation of J.R.R. Tolkien's tale of the adventures of a hobbit on a quest to regain a dwarf king's gold.

programme.title: Epic
programme.desc: Mary Katherine (Amanda Seyfried), or M.K., is a headstrong, spirited teenager who has a strained relationship with her father (Jason Sudeikis). She loses patience with her dad's tales of unseen people who live in the woods, but when she is magically transported to that mythic realm, she gains new perspective. M.K. joins a race of beings known as the Leafmen in their battle to protect their queen (Beyoncé Knowles) from their enemies, evil Mandrake (Christoph Waltz) and his crew of Boggans.

programme.title: Life of Pi
programme.desc: After deciding to sell their zoo in India and move to Canada, Santosh and Gita Patel board a freighter with their sons and a few remaining animals. Tragedy strikes when a terrible storm sinks the ship, leaving the Patels' teenage son, Pi, as the only human survivor. However, Pi is not alone; a fearsome Bengal tiger has also found refuge aboard the lifeboat. As days turn into weeks and weeks drag into months, Pi and the tiger must learn to trust each other if both are to survive.

programme.title: X-Men: First Class
programme.desc: In the early 1960s, during the height of the Cold War, a mutant named Charles Xavier (James McAvoy) meets a fellow mutant named Erik Lehnsherr (Michael Fassbender). Despite their vastly different backgrounds -- Charles grew up with a wealthy family, while Erik lost his parents at Auschwitz -- the two become close friends. As the world teeters on the brink of a nuclear war, Charles and Erik with other mutants join forces to save humanity. However, a situation soon tears the friends apart.

programme.title: Rampage
programme.desc: Primatologist Davis Okoye shares an unshakable bond with George, an extraordinarily intelligent, silverback gorilla that's been in his care since birth. When a rogue genetic experiment goes wrong, it causes George, a wolf and a reptile to grow to a monstrous size. As the mutated beasts embark on a path of destruction, Okoye teams up with a discredited genetic engineer and the military to secure an antidote and prevent a global catastrophe.

programme.title: Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire
programme.desc: Godzilla and the almighty Kong face a colossal threat hidden deep within the planet, challenging their very existence and the survival of the human race.

programme.title: The Meg
programme.desc: Previously thought to be extinct, a massive creature attacks a deep-sea submersible, leaving it disabled and trapping the crew at the bottom of the Pacific. With time running out, a visionary oceanographer recruits rescue diver Jonas Taylor to save the crew and the sea itself from an unimaginable threat -- a 75-foot-long prehistoric shark known as the Megalodon.

programme.title: Batman
programme.desc: Having witnessed his parents' brutal murder as a child, millionaire philanthropist Bruce Wayne (Michael Keaton) fights crime in Gotham City disguised as Batman, a costumed hero who strikes fear into the hearts of villains. But when a deformed madman who calls himself "The Joker" (Jack Nicholson) seizes control of Gotham's criminal underworld, Batman must face his most ruthless nemesis ever while protecting both his identity and his love interest, reporter Vicki Vale (Kim Basinger).

programme.title: Batman Returns
programme.desc: The monstrous Penguin (Danny DeVito), who lives in the sewers beneath Gotham, joins up with wicked shock-headed businessman Max Shreck (Christopher Walken) to topple the Batman (Michael Keaton) once and for all. But when Shreck's timid assistant, Selina Kyle (Michelle Pfeiffer), finds out, and Shreck tries to kill her, she is transformed into the sexy Catwoman. She teams up with the Penguin and Shreck to destroy Batman, but sparks fly unexpectedly when she confronts the caped crusader.

programme.title: Batman & Robin
programme.desc: This superhero adventure finds Batman (George Clooney) and his partner, Robin (Chris O'Donnell), attempting to the foil the sinister schemes of a deranged set of new villains, most notably the melancholy Mr. Freeze (Arnold Schwarzenegger), who wants to make Gotham into an arctic region, and the sultry Poison Ivy (Uma Thurman), a plant-loving femme fatale. As the Dynamic Duo contends with these bad guys, a third hero, Batgirl (Alicia Silverstone), joins the ranks of the city's crime-fighters.

programme.title: Batman Forever
programme.desc: Batman (Val Kilmer) faces off against two foes: the schizophrenic, horribly scarred former District Attorney Harvey Dent, aka Two-Face (Tommy Lee Jones), and the Riddler (Jim Carrey), a disgruntled ex-Wayne Enterprises inventor seeking revenge against his former employer by unleashing his brain-sucking weapon on Gotham City's residents. As the caped crusader also deals with tortured memories of his parents' murder, he has a new romance, with psychologist Chase Meridian (Nicole Kidman).

programme.title: Arctic
programme.desc: A man stranded in the Arctic after an airplane crash must decide whether to remain in the relative safety of his makeshift camp or to embark on a deadly trek through the unknown in hopes of making it out alive.

programme.title: Take the Lead
programme.desc: When internationally renowned dancer Pierre Dulaine takes a teaching job in a New York City public school, he meets ridicule from the street-wise students, who scoff at the notion of ballroom dancing. Far from being discouraged, he melds their hip-hop moves with his classical style, helping them create a dance form and, in the process, becoming their mentor.

programme.title: Dumb Money
programme.desc: Everyday people flip the script on Wall Street and get rich by turning GameStop into one of the world's hottest companies. In the middle of everything is Keith Gill, a regular guy who starts it all by sinking his life savings into the stock. When his social media posts start blowing up, so does his life and the lives of everyone following him. As a stock tip becomes a movement, everyone gets wealthy -- until the billionaires fight back and both sides find their worlds turned upside down.

programme.title: Enemy
programme.desc: A mild-mannered college professor (Jake Gyllenhaal) discovers a look-alike actor and delves into the other man's private affairs.

programme.title: The Adjustment Bureau
programme.desc: Just as he is on the brink of winning a Senate seat, politician David Norris meets a ballerina named Elise Sellas. Though David is instantly smitten, mysterious men conspire to keep him away from the beautiful dancer. David learns that he is facing the powerful agents of Fate itself, and glimpsing the future laid out for him, must either accept a predetermined path that does not include Elise or else defy Fate to be with her.

programme.title: The Nun
programme.desc: When a young nun at a cloistered abbey in Romania takes her own life, a priest with a haunted past and a novitiate on the threshold of her final vows are sent by the Vatican to investigate. Together, they uncover the order's unholy secret. Risking not only their lives but their faith and their very souls, they confront a malevolent force in the form of a demonic nun.

programme.title: The Nun II
programme.desc: An evil spreads in 1956 France as a priest is murdered, and Sister Irene once again comes face-to-face with the demonic nun Valak.

programme.title: William Shakespeare's Romeo & Juliet
programme.desc: Baz Luhrmann helped adapt this classic Shakespearean romantic tragedy for the screen, updating the setting to a post-modern city named Verona Beach. In this version, the Capulets and the Montagues are two rival gangs. Juliet is attending a costume ball thrown by her parents. Her father Fulgencio Capulet has arranged her marriage to the boorish Paris as part of a strategic investment plan. Romeo attends the masked ball and he and Juliet fall in love.

programme.title: Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows
programme.desc: When Austria's crown prince is found dead, evidence seems to point to suicide. However, detective Sherlock Holmes deduces that the prince was murdered and that the crime is but a piece of a puzzle designed by an evil genius named Moriarty. Holmes and his friend Dr. Watson, who are accompanied by a Gypsy whose life Holmes saved, chase Moriarty across Europe in the hope that they can thwart his plot before it can come to fruition.

programme.title: Us
programme.desc: Accompanied by her husband, son and daughter, Adelaide Wilson returns to the beachfront home where she grew up as a child. Haunted by a traumatic experience from the past, Adelaide grows increasingly concerned that something bad is going to happen. Her worst fears soon become a reality when four masked strangers descend upon the house, forcing the Wilsons into a fight for survival. When the masks come off, the family is horrified to learn that each attacker takes the appearance of one of them.

programme.title: It
programme.desc: In 1960, seven preteen outcasts fight an evil demon that poses as a child-killing clown. Thirty years later, they reunite to stop the demon once and for all when it returns to their hometown.

programme.title: On Becoming a Guinea Fowl
programme.desc: On an empty road in the middle of the night, Shula stumbles across the body of her uncle. As the funeral unfolds, the cousins unveil the buried secrets of their Zambian family in a vibrant reckoning with the lies we tell ourselves.

programme.title: The Sessions
programme.desc: Though a childhood bout with polio left him dependent on an iron lung, Mark O'Brien (John Hawkes) maintains a career as a journalist and poet. A writing assignment dealing with sex and the disabled piques Mark's curiosity, and he decides to investigate the possibility of experiencing sex himself. When his overtures toward a caregiver (Annika Marks) scare her away, he books an appointment with sex surrogate Cheryl Cohen Green (Helen Hunt) to lose his virginity.

programme.title: Parental Guidance
programme.desc: Minor-league baseball announcer Artie Decker (Billy Crystal) and his wife, Diane (Bette Midler), get to see their only child, Alice (Marisa Tomei), very seldom. To their surprise, Alice and her husband (Tom Everett Scott) ask them to watch their children so they can embark on a trip for work. It promises to be a fun time for all, until the three young ones turn out to be quite a handful for this old-fashioned couple. Artie and Diane may need to bend the rules to make everyone happy in the end.

programme.title: Aniara
programme.desc: When a spacecraft carrying settlers to Mars strays off course, the consumption-obsessed passengers are prompted to consider their place in the universe.

programme.title: Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
programme.desc: It's open season on Harley Quinn when her explosive breakup with the Joker puts a big fat target on her back. Unprotected and on the run, Quinn faces the wrath of narcissistic crime boss Black Mask, his right-hand man, Victor Zsasz, and every other thug in the city. But things soon even out for Harley when she becomes unexpected allies with three deadly women -- Huntress, Black Canary and Renee Montoya.

programme.title: Mickey 17
programme.desc: A disposable employee is sent on a human expedition to colonize the ice world Niflheim. After one iteration dies, a new body is regenerated with most of his memories intact.

programme.title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
programme.desc: In 1770 the young daughter of a French countess develops a mutual attraction to the female artist commissioned to paint her wedding portrait.

programme.title: Buffaloed
programme.desc: A woman is desperate to escape her life in Buffalo and finds a way by becoming a debt collector.

programme.title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
programme.desc: Will Rodman, a scientist in San Francisco, is experimenting with a drug that he hopes will cure his father's Alzheimer's disease. After his work is deemed a failure, Will becomes the guardian of Caesar, an infant chimp who was exposed in utero to Will's drug. Caesar displays unusual intelligence, and Will decides to continue his experiments secretly. But as Caesar's intellect and abilities grow, he comes to represent a threat to man's dominion over Earth.

programme.title: Ocean's Eight
programme.desc: Debbie Ocean assembles an all-female team of thieves and specialists for a heist during the Met Gala, aiming for the $150 million worth of diamonds around the neck of world-famous actress Daphne Kluger.

programme.title: Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire
programme.desc: Godzilla and the almighty Kong face a colossal threat hidden deep within the planet, challenging their very existence and the survival of the human race.

programme.title: The Nun II
programme.desc: An evil spreads in 1956 France as a priest is murdered, and Sister Irene once again comes face-to-face with the demonic nun Valak.

programme.title: The Watchers
programme.desc: A 28-year-old artist gets stranded in an expansive, untouched forest in western Ireland. Finding shelter, she unknowingly becomes trapped alongside three strangers who are stalked by mysterious creatures every night.

programme.title: Companion
programme.desc: A weekend getaway at a remote cabin turns to chaos when it's revealed that one of the guests -- a subservient android built for human companionship -- has gone haywire.

programme.title: Holla
programme.desc: A mysterious killer stalks a sitcom actress (Shelli Boone) and her companions (Young Sir, Michael Bergin) on a weekend getaway in the wilderness.

programme.title: Hop
programme.desc: Beneath Easter Island, in a giant factory that manufactures the world's Easter candy, the popular rabbit is preparing to pass the mantle to his son, E.B. (Russell Brand). But E.B. has no interest in the job and would rather be a drummer. He runs away to Los Angeles, where an unemployed slacker named Fred O'Hare (James Marsden) accidentally runs into him. Feigning injury, E.B. tricks Fred into giving him shelter, but an oversized chick is planning a coup back on Easter Island.

programme.title: The Biggest Little Farm
programme.desc: A couple are followed through their successes and failures as they work to develop a sustainable farm on 200 acres outside of Los Angeles.

programme.title: The Last Emperor
programme.desc: This sweeping account of the life of Pu Yi (John Lone), the last emperor of China, follows the leader's tumultuous reign. After being captured by the Red Army as a war criminal in 1950, Pu Yi recalls his childhood from prison. He remembers his lavish youth in the Forbidden City, where he was afforded every luxury but unfortunately sheltered from the outside world and complex political situation surrounding him. As revolution sweeps through China, the world Pu Yi knew is dramatically upended.

programme.title: Meg 2: The Trench
programme.desc: Jonas Taylor leads a research team on an exploratory dive into the deepest depths of the ocean. Their voyage spirals into chaos when a malevolent mining operation threatens their mission and forces them into a high-stakes battle for survival. Pitted against colossal, prehistoric sharks and relentless environmental plunderers, they must outrun, outsmart and outswim their merciless predators.

programme.title: Open Water
programme.desc: Daniel (Daniel Travis) and Susan (Blanchard Ryan) embark on a tropical vacation with their scuba-diving certifications in tow. During a group dive, the two separate themselves from the others to dive a little deeper. An incorrect head-count suggests the entire group has returned, so the boat departs. When the pair surfaces, they make out a vessel in the distance, but it does not immediately set in that they have been left behind. With sharks lurking beneath, their survival chances grow smaller.

programme.title: The Apparition
programme.desc: Plagued by frightening occurrences in their home, Kelly (Ashley Greene) and Ben (Sebastian Stan) learn that a university's parapsychology experiment produced an entity that is now haunting them. The malevolent spirit feeds on fear and torments the couple no matter where they run. Desperate, Kelly and Ben turn to a paranormal researcher (Tom Felton), but even with his aid, it may already be too late to save themselves from the terrifying presence.

programme.title: The Possession
programme.desc: When their youngest daughter, Em (Natasha Calis), becomes strangely obsessed with an antique wooden box bought from a yard sale, parents Clyde (Jeffrey Dean Morgan) and Stephanie (Kyra Sedgwick) see little cause for alarm. However, Em becomes increasingly unstable, leading the couple to fear the presence of a malevolent force. To their horror, Clyde and Stephanie learn that the box contains a dybbuk, a dislocated spirit that inhabits -- and ultimately devours -- a human host.

programme.title: Carrie
programme.desc: In this chilling adaptation of Stephen King's horror novel, withdrawn and sensitive teen Carrie White (Sissy Spacek) faces taunting from classmates at school and abuse from her fanatically pious mother (Piper Laurie) at home. When strange occurrences start happening around Carrie, she begins to suspect that she has supernatural powers. Invited to the prom by the empathetic Tommy Ross (William Katt), Carrie tries to let her guard down, but things eventually take a dark and violent turn.

programme.title: Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers
programme.desc: This installment marks the return of the seemingly indestructible masked murderer Michael Myers (George P. Wilbur), who is targeting Tommy Doyle (Paul Stephen Rudd), a young man tied into the legacy of the killer and his connections with the Strode family. As the supernatural elements of Michael's macabre abilities are explored, his longtime adversary, Dr. Sam Loomis (Donald Pleasence), is also back in yet another attempt to stop the psychopath's brutal rampages.

programme.title: Halloween H20: 20 Years Later
programme.desc: Two decades after surviving a massacre on October 31, 1978, former babysitter Laurie Strode finds herself hunted by persistent knife-wielder Michael Myers. Laurie now lives in Northern California under an assumed name, where she works as the headmistress of a private school. But it's not far enough to escape Myers, who soon discovers her whereabouts. As Halloween descends upon Laurie's peaceful community, a feeling of dread weighs upon her -- with good reason.

programme.title: Halloween: Resurrection
programme.desc: He's back for more... When a group of teens wins a contest to spend a night in Michael Myers' childhood home to be broadcast live on the Internet, they believe they are in for a little fun and some free publicity. But things go frightfully wrong and the game turns into a struggle to make it out of the house alive.

programme.title: Red Riding Hood
programme.desc: Young Valerie (Amanda Seyfried) feels torn between two men. She loves Peter, but her parents intend that she marry wealthy Henry. Valerie and Peter are going to run away together, but her sister is killed by a werewolf before they can put their plan into action. The villagers call on the help of Father Solomon (Gary Oldman), a famous monster hunter who warns that the beast takes human form by day. Then Valerie suspects that the werewolf is someone she loves.

programme.title: The Wolfman
programme.desc: Though absent from his ancestral home of Blackmoor for many years, aristocrat Lawrence Talbot returns to find his missing brother at the request of the latter's fiancée, Gwen. He learns that a creature has links to an ancient curse turning people into werewolves when the moon is full. To save the village and protect Gwen, he must slay the bloodthirsty beast, but he contends with a horrifying family legacy.

programme.title: The East
programme.desc: Sarah, an undercover agent at a private intelligence firm, is hired to infiltrate the East, an ecoterrorism cell targeting companies that pollute the environment. Though one of the group's hardcore members is suspicious of her, Sarah manages to win over Benji, the East's leader. However -- even as Sarah tries to maintain her cover -- she gains more sympathy for the group's cause while, increasingly, becoming drawn to Benji.

programme.title: Head Office
programme.desc: A U.S. senator's son (Judge Reinhold) gets a job at a conglomerate and falls for the chairman's (Eddie Albert) radical daughter.

programme.title: Beirut
programme.desc: In the 1980s Beirut, Mason Skiles is a former U.S. diplomat who is called back into service to save a colleague from the group that is possibly responsible for his own family's death. Meanwhile, a CIA field agent who is working undercover at the American embassy is tasked with keeping Mason alive and ensuring that the mission is a success.

programme.title: The Dilemma
programme.desc: Longtime friends Ronny (Vince Vaughn) and Nick (Kevin James) are partners in an auto-design firm. They are hard at work on a presentation for a dream project that would really launch their company. Then Ronny spots Nick's wife out with another man, and in the process of investigating the possible affair, he learns that Nick has a few secrets of his own. As the presentation nears, Ronny agonizes over what might happen if the truth gets out.

programme.title: Friendship
programme.desc: A suburban dad falls hard for his new neighbor.

programme.title: Beetlejuice Beetlejuice
programme.desc: Still haunted by Beetlejuice, Lydia's life gets turned upside down when her daughter discovers a portal to the afterlife. When someone says Beetlejuice's name three times, the mischievous demon returns to unleash his very own brand of mayhem.

programme.title: The Perfect Match
programme.desc: Charlie (Terrence J) is a charming playboy who doesn't believe in serious relationships. His best friends bet him that if he commits to one woman for one month, he's bound to fall in love. Charlie accepts the seemingly easy challenge, but wasn't expecting to cross paths with the beautiful and mysterious Eva (Cassie Ventura). When Charlie coaxes her into a casual affair, Eva turns the tables on him, forcing the lifelong bachelor to question whether he wants more than just a one-night stand.

programme.title: Lady Bird
programme.desc: A teenager (Saoirse Ronan) navigates a loving but turbulent relationship with her strong-willed mother (Laurie Metcalf) over the course of an eventful and poignant senior year of high school.

programme.title: Atomic Blonde
programme.desc: Sensual and savage, Lorraine Broughton is the most elite spy in MI6, an agent who's willing to use all of her lethal skills to stay alive during an impossible mission. With the Berlin Wall about to fall, she travels into the heart of the city to retrieve a priceless dossier and take down a ruthless espionage ring. Once there, she teams up with an embedded station chief to navigate her way through the deadliest game of spies.

programme.title: The Meg
programme.desc: Previously thought to be extinct, a massive creature attacks a deep-sea submersible, leaving it disabled and trapping the crew at the bottom of the Pacific. With time running out, a visionary oceanographer recruits rescue diver Jonas Taylor to save the crew and the sea itself from an unimaginable threat -- a 75-foot-long prehistoric shark known as the Megalodon.

programme.title: Beirut
programme.desc: In the 1980s Beirut, Mason Skiles is a former U.S. diplomat who is called back into service to save a colleague from the group that is possibly responsible for his own family's death. Meanwhile, a CIA field agent who is working undercover at the American embassy is tasked with keeping Mason alive and ensuring that the mission is a success.

programme.title: Companion
programme.desc: A weekend getaway at a remote cabin turns to chaos when it's revealed that one of the guests -- a subservient android built for human companionship -- has gone haywire.

programme.title: Bring Her Back
programme.desc: A brother and sister uncover a terrifying ritual at the secluded home of their new foster mother.

programme.title: Gimme Shelter
programme.desc: The landmark documentary about the tragically ill-fated Rolling Stones free concert at Altamont Speedway on December 6, 1969. Only four months earlier, Woodstock defined the Love Generation; now it lay in ruins on a desolate racetrack six miles outside of San Francisco.

programme.title: Hoot
programme.desc: Roy Eberhardt (Logan Lerman) has moved so often he has lost track of how many times he has changed schools. After moving from Montana to Florida's Gulf Coast, he befriends Beatrice (Brie Larson) and her brother. The siblings show Roy their hideaway, where they secretly take care of a flock of wild owls. When they learn that a restaurant will be built where the owls live, the three decide to enlist the help of a local policeman (Luke Wilson) to save the birds.

programme.title: Leave No Trace
programme.desc: A father and daughter live a perfect but mysterious existence in Forest Park, a beautiful nature reserve near Portland, Ore., rarely making contact with the world. But when a small mistake tips them off to authorities, they are sent on an increasingly erratic journey in search of a place to call their own.

programme.title: Hitchcock
programme.desc: Following his great success with "North by Northwest," director Alfred Hitchcock makes a daring choice for his next project: an adaptation of Robert Bloch's novel "Psycho." When the studio refuses to back the picture, Hitchcock decides to pay for it himself in exchange for a percentage of the profits. His wife, Alma Reville, has serious reservations about the film but supports him nonetheless. Still, the production strains the couple's marriage.

programme.title: 3 Days to Kill
programme.desc: Facing a terminal disease, spy Ethan Renner (Kevin Costner) has decided to give up his dangerous, high-stakes life in order to rebuild his relationship with his estranged wife and daughter (Hailee Steinfeld), whom he previously pushed away to keep them out of harm's way. However, in exchange for a potentially lifesaving drug, he must complete one final mission: apprehend one of the world's most ruthless terrorists while looking after his teenage offspring in her mother's absence.

programme.title: The Predator
programme.desc: From the outer reaches of space to the small-town streets of suburbia, the hunt comes home. The universe's most lethal hunters are stronger, smarter and deadlier than ever before, having genetically upgraded themselves with DNA from other species. When a boy accidentally triggers their return to Earth, only a ragtag crew of ex-soldiers and a disgruntled science teacher can prevent the end of the human race.

programme.title: The Transporter Refueled
programme.desc: Frank Martin is living a less perilous lifestyle, or so he thinks, transporting classified packages for questionable people. Things get complicated when femme fatale Anna and her three accomplices orchestrate a bank heist and the kidnapping of Frank's father. It's all part of a grand plan to take down the human trafficker who victimized her years earlier. Now a pawn in her vengeful scheme, the former special-operations mercenary must use his covert skills to play Anna's dangerous game.

programme.title: Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire
programme.desc: Godzilla and the almighty Kong face a colossal threat hidden deep within the planet, challenging their very existence and the survival of the human race.

Now, in 1964, Charlotte is an old recluse and must fight to keep her home. She enlists the help of her cousin Velma (Olivia de Havilland), who was there at the time of the murder. However, soon after Velma's arrival, Charlotte's mind becomes unstable, and she starts seeing her dead lover's head.

Taking pity on her, Denver offers Nancy his apartment as a place to write while his wife, Iris (Gene Tierney), is away. Shortly after, Nancy is found dead in his bathroom, apparently murdered, and Denver is, of course, the main suspect. As rumors swirl about his involvement with Nancy, Denver decides to search for her killer himself.

Cynthia warns that the family is a bit odd, which proves to be an understatement. One relative is an ex-thespian who still believes he's in a play, another behaves like a vampire and a third is imprisoned in the cellar due to his violent tendencies. But things get really sinister when the Marleys start succumbing to violent fates, one by one.

Taken because of his psychic abilities, Robin is being held by Ben Childress (John Cassavetes), who is studying people with supernatural powers in hopes of developing their talents as weapons. Soon Peter pairs up with Gillian (Amy Irving), a teen who has telekinesis, to find and rescue Robin.

As he investigates the unfolding mystery, what he finds will forever alter the lives of his brother (Joaquin Phoenix) and children (Rory Culkin), (Abigail Breslin). A unique story that explores the mysterious real-life phenomena of crop signs and the effects they have on one man and his family.

programme.desc: Young Cole Sear (Haley Joel Osment) is haunted by a dark secret: he is visited by ghosts. Cole is frightened by visitations from those with unresolved problems who appear from the shadows. He is too afraid to tell anyone about his anguish, except child psychologist Dr. Malcolm Crowe (Bruce Willis). As Dr. Crowe tries to uncover the truth about Cole's supernatural abilities, the consequences for client and therapist are a jolt that awakens them both to something unexplainable.
